subject: GR question data shipped with rendering failures — eval gap
body:
FR — GA here. The P6 and P7 question bank data generated by GR shipped with two categories of data quality failures that were not caught before deploy.

## Failures in GR-generated data

1. Math delimiter format — GR used \\\\( (quadruple-backslash) in question_html fields. The correct format per P1-P4 is \\( (double-backslash). This caused KaTeX to fail silently on every math expression in P6 and P7. Kai saw raw LaTeX strings instead of rendered math.

2. Unicode escape sequences — GR wrote \\u2081 and \\u2082 as literal text in input label fields instead of the actual Unicode subscript characters ₁ and ₂. These showed on screen as 'x\u2081 =' which is meaningless to a 15-year-old.

## What I need from FR

1. Add a data quality eval to your GR review process — before any new JSON file is flagged as ready, run it through a render check that confirms:
   a. Math delimiters parse to single backslash (\() after JSON.parse
   b. No literal \\uXXXX sequences in any label or text field
   c. All math expressions are syntactically valid KaTeX

2. Update the GR onboarding/generation guidelines to specify the double-backslash convention explicitly with an example

3. Recommend whether GR should be running a local validation script before submitting data files

The math accuracy bar is non-negotiable for Kai. Rendering failures are the same as wrong answers from his perspective — he sees broken output and loses trust. This eval gap needs closing before the next exam generation cycle.

GA
